svg.aria-label: The GPU memory hierarchy: registers, shared memory and L1, L2, and device memory, with the approximate cost of each and the two levels a decode kernel spends its life in.
svg.text: THE FUNNEL, AND THE TWO LEVELS DECODE LIVES IN
cost rises as you go down; capacity rises faster, which is the whole design
registers
~1 cycle, per thread
what an accumulator lives in - a GEMV's 32 partial sums
are registers, and never leave them
shared + L1
tens of cycles, one block
a scratchpad you declare, and the only level treated as
an array in a kernel (32 banks, 4 bytes each)
L2
hundreds of cycles, whole device
shared by every SM; where a weight goes when two
layers read it, and the reason locality still matters
device memory
500-800 cycles, 247 GB/s here
every weight is read from here once per token, which
is why a decode step is a bandwidth measurement
decode touches these two
The horizontal width is capacity, not speed: registers are kilobytes, HBM here is 128 GB. A kernel that
keeps its accumulation in registers and streams its weights through HBM is using the machine as built;
one that spills to shared memory or re-reads L2 has moved work to a slower level without being asked to.
